findings.title: A link to /tools/satake/ fetches 92297 B of JavaScript before the first interaction: T13 loads its typeset-name chunk while the island hydrates (166 of the 167 Atlas links)
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T13SatakeStudio.svelte:325-330 (the hydration $effect calls readLink), :311-321 (readLink calls setConfig when the link names another pair) and :303-308 (setConfig calls loadNames); site/src/components/tools/t13/names.ts:15-21 (loadNames imports t13/satakeNames.ts, chunk _astro/satakeNames.*.js)
findings.claim: When the URL names a pair other than the configured one, T13's hydration effect goes through setConfig, which calls loadNames. The typeset-name chunk (5230 B gzip) is then fetched with no input, so /tools/satake/ opened from a link fetches 92297 B before the reader's first interaction, over the 90 kB of a tool alone. /embed/satake/ behaves the same.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.6: a tool alone on /tools/<id> stays within 90 kB, counted as 'all JavaScript the route fetches before the reader's first interaction'. SPEC 6.6: on a tool's own route the link keys are bare, so a link opens the same route. decisions/P6-A3.md ('the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily'): the names load 'in the browser only after the reader's first change of decoration or of panel ..., because the section weighs about 5 kB gzipped and the route measured 85.0 of its 90 kB without it'.
findings.observed: Root preview build of f07eec6: the default /tools/satake/ is 87067 B (18 scripts); 166 of the 167 'Open this real form in the Satake Studio' links on the 32 Atlas pages each measure 92297 B, with the only extra script satakeNames.MjFZAB5c.js at 5230 B. The exception is the link equal to the default pair, A3 x=2 t=3.2.1, at 87067 B. The E7 and E8 links also fetch the worker script (24098 B, not counted). The committed spec fails on its 3 link cases with 'Expected <= 90000, Received 92297' ('scripts beyond the default state: satakeNames.MjFZAB5c.js 5230'); its control (the default route) passes. npm run size cannot see this, because it opens bare routes only.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of f07eec6 plus this branch: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<pw> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-playwright.config.ts redteam-RT-07-p6-link-size.spec.ts. Result: 3 failed (links A3 x=1.3, D8 x=1.3.5.7, E6 x=2.3.4.5), 1 passed (control). The config hard-codes this worktree's path in WT; edit WT for another checkout. The full sweep: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<pw> node redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-link-sweep.mjs site/dist / 5572 <scratch>/links.json /satake/ 3 prints '167 links measured; 166 over the limit of their route'.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 (table row 'each tool alone, on /tools/<id> | 90 kB'; 'all JavaScript the route fetches before the reader's first interaction'); SPEC.md 6.6 ('On a tool's own route (/tools/..., /embed/...) the keys are bare'); decisions/P6-A3.md 2026-10-25 'the names of real forms, typeset at build time and loaded lazily'
findings.proposedFix: Fetch the names only from the reader's own actions (paint, tau, pick, example, catalogue entry, openPanel). readLink should load the link's pair without loadNames, keeping the plain-markup names that names.ts already writes until the first change. Adopting the committed spec keeps a link state under 90 kB, which npm run size does not check.

findings.location: site/src/content/pages/glossary.mdx (P6-A8: 83 entries, 185 formulas, 430 dd); site/astro.config.mjs:59 and site/src/lib/katex.ts:20 (KaTeX output htmlAndMathml); site/src/layouts/Page.astro:119-130

findings.title: T12.spec.ts:1242, the test that failed gate G6, cannot tell a regression from noise: it times T12's own hydration, about 35 to 65 ms at full speed for any link that changes the state, its control included, in G5 and G6 alike
findings.location: site/tests/e2e/T12.spec.ts:1207-1238 (hydrationTask returns 0 for a task under 50 ms) and :1241-1255 (median of three; limit max(50, control + 15)); site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:742-763 (readLink and load(state) run inside the hydration $effect)
findings.claim: The case (C8 node 7) and the control (E7 node 7, 56 positions) hydrate in tasks of the same length: Svelte's hydration of the server markup plus the re-render to the link's state, with 14 to 20 ms of engine facts. Those tasks straddle 50 ms on this container. Because the test maps every task under 50 ms to 0, the control's median usually collapses to 0 while the case's lands on 51 to 64 at random. Phase 6 added nothing measurable to the task.
findings.expected: The test's stated purpose (from P5-RT-07-01): a link to a large orbit must not hydrate in a longer task than a small one. SPEC 7.6: 'No engine call on the main thread may become a long task (50 ms)'. A regression test should fail only when the behaviour regresses.
findings.observed: True task lengths from traces, 5 runs alternated G5 (6cd2c06) against G6 (f07eec6), RATE=1, medians in ms. At load 23 to 26: C8:7 G5 76.6 [141, 54.3, 52.8, 116.4, 76.6], G6 51.3 [46.1, 127.1, 110.9, 51.3, 39.3]; E7:7 control G5 49.3, G6 42.5; no link G5 28.0, G6 25.5. At load 11 to 15: C8:7 G5 41.5, G6 53.4; E7:7 G5 65.3, G6 51.3; no link G5 34.7, G6 33.3. Module evaluation inside the task is 1 to 4 ms in both builds. Profile (source maps, 1x): Svelte runtime 59 to 62 ms inclusive of a 66 to 70 ms task (with the profiler running); engine self 13.6 to 19.9 ms (startRepresentation, minusculeNodes, orbitSize, classify of C8). No minusculeMatrices or signedMoves run, so the P5 fix holds. The phase 5 reproducer, longtask-based: control E7:7 median 55 [50, 55, 70] at load 24 and 53 [0, 53, 116] at load 15; C8:7 64 and 0. findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.6 'Main-thread work'; site/tests/e2e/T12.spec.ts regression P5-RT-07-01; reports/gate-G6.md section 12; build-plan/reports/orchestrator/round-p5/fixout/confirm-t12-perf.json
findings.proposedFix: Either measure what the test means: time the engine calls inside the hydration task (a performance.measure around readLink and the T12Tool construction, or a CPU profile), or compare true task lengths from a trace for case and control. Or change the product: run load(state) for a link in a task after hydration, so that the hydration task holds only the server markup (about 25 to 35 ms) and the link's re-render gets a task of its own.

findings.title: T13 classifies the same board two or three times on every board load: satakeRecord classifies a fresh board on each matchCatalogue call, and T13 keeps its own board objects beside the site's
findings.location: packages/engine/src/satakeCatalogue.ts:268 and :271 (satakeRecord builds boardFromName(name) and guards it on every call); packages/engine/src/satake.ts:171 (guard(d.board) on T13's board object); site/src/components/tools/t13/model.ts:67-73 (T13's own boardOf map); site/src/lib/state.ts:174 (verdictOf on resolveBoard's object at load)
findings.claim: A T13 board load computes classify for three different objects of the same board: the site's resolveBoard object, T13's own boardOf object, and a fresh object that satakeRecord builds at every matchCatalogue call. A pick computes it twice. This is the sibling of P5-RT-07-02 in the new tool.
findings.expected: SPEC 5.6: 'A tool decides whether a board is of finite type by calling classify once when the board is loaded'. E-11 keeps the verdict per board object. RT-FIX P5-RT-07-02 used one board object per name for T12.
findings.observed: classifyUncached computations, counted by a logpoint placed through the source map of a sourcemap build. /tools/satake/ load (A3): 3. Picks D8, E6, B3, G2: 2 each. A link to D8: 3 for D8 (plus 3 for the default A3). M9 load (A1): 3. T12 for comparison: 1 per pick. The stacks map to state.ts:174 verdictOf, satake.ts:171 guard and satakeCatalogue.ts:271 guard. Cost per extra classify is small: 0.07 to 0.14 ms in Node (C8 0.14).
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; OUT_DIR=<scratch>/dist-maps node node_modules/astro/bin/astro.mjs build --root <wt>/site --config ../redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-sourcemap.config.mjs; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<pw> ONLY=satake STACKS=1 node redteam/redteam-RT-07-p6-classify-count.mjs <scratch>/dist-maps 5571 (exit 1; 'MORE THAN ONE classify per board load' lists the T13 loads and picks)
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 5.6 last sentence; SPEC.md 5.1 E-11; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-25 'RT-FIX-P5-t12-perf: one board object per name in T12 (P5-RT-07-02)'
findings.proposedFix: Let satakeRecord (and finiteBoard) reuse one board object per name, through a module map in satakeCatalogue.ts or by taking the caller's board. Have T13 take its board objects from lib/state.ts resolveBoard, so that the page holds one object per name, as T12 does.

notes: Gate G6's T12 failure has no phase 6 cause (finding 04). The engine work of P5-RT-07-01 stays out of the hydration task. G5 and G6 hydrate T12 in tasks of the same length, and its control is as long as its case.

Static pages and Lighthouse: on pages with no script, TBT measures where FCP falls relative to one large layout, not how much work there is. The gate, on an idle machine, had FCP early and TBT high (glossary 432.4). My runs under load 14 to 30 had LCP at 0.9 to 1.6 s and TBT 0 to 86, except one run at LCP 663 ms with TBT 661. With 3 runs per route (decisions/P3-A7.md), Atlas pages swing from 0 to 310 between runs. For the owner's lab item: of the 20 routes over at G6, the 3 static ones (/glossary/, /sources/, /atlas/C7/) have this cause. /sources/ (283437 B, 5982 elements, 204 formulas) is the same size class and predates phase 6.

T13 instances configured on E6 in M9 (b7, b11, b12, client:visible) hydrate, when scrolled into view at 1x (load 25), in one task of 80 to 251 ms: b7 median 134, b11 117. The A3 instance b2 shows no long task. Profile: about 34 to 36 ms of that task is engine (computeNow runs satake, restrictedBoard and matchCatalogue at once, plus admissibility); the rest is T13's own hydration. Not reported as a finding: the long task is mostly rendering, E6 is in the owner-held E-9 sizing, and lab TBT does not cover scroll hydration. It belongs to the owner's phone check of Interaction to Next Paint. In Node at load 21, T13's three data calls take at most 13.2 ms in all on a non-held board (B5 so(11)) and 27.5 on a held one (C8 sp(8)).
